questions.text: Only what is needed for the work in this area is here.
questions.help: Look for spare parts, tools, packaging, paperwork and personal items with no job to do.

questions.text: The red tag process is used: unneeded items are tagged, with an owner and a decision date.
questions.help: Check the red tag area and the register. Tags should not sit for weeks without a decision.

questions.text: Materials at the point of use are only what the current job needs.
questions.help: Packaging, film, cartons and consumables beyond the current run should be back in their store.

questions.text: No broken, obsolete or unused equipment, jigs or spares are kept in the area.
questions.help: Look under benches, behind guards and on top of cabinets.

questions.text: Food, drinks and personal belongings are only in designated places.
questions.help: Check against the hygiene and allergen rules for the area.

questions.text: Every item has a defined home that is marked or labelled.
questions.help: Floor marking, shadow boards, shelf labels or location signs. Could a new starter see where each thing goes?

questions.text: Items are in their home and the area matches the standard layout.
questions.help: Compare with the standard layout. Anything out of place, missing or extra counts against this.

questions.text: Stock and consumables have marked minimum and maximum levels, and they are respected.
questions.help: Look for overfilled racks, empty locations and unmarked quantities.

questions.text: Walkways, fire points, electrical panels and emergency exits are marked and kept clear.
questions.help: Check aisle widths, truck routes, and clearance in front of panels and extinguishers.

questions.text: Tools and materials can be found and fetched without searching.
questions.help: Ask the operator to fetch three items and note how long it takes.

questions.text: Floors, machines and surfaces are clean, with no build-up of product, dust or spills.
questions.help: Check corners, under guards, drip trays, and the tops of machines.

questions.text: Cleaning and inspection routines are defined, visible and signed off.
questions.help: Look at cleaning schedules, checklists and the dates they were signed.

questions.text: Leaks, spills and sources of contamination are found, tagged and being fixed.
questions.help: Repeat dirt in the same place points to a cause that needs fixing, not just cleaning.

questions.text: Lighting, guards, covers, labels and signs are clean and undamaged.
questions.help: Check that nothing is obscured, cracked or missing.

questions.text: Cleaning equipment is stored in its home, in good condition and colour coded where required.
questions.help: Brushes, mops, scoops and cloths. Check allergen and hygiene colour coding.

questions.text: Visual standards are displayed and current: layout, marking colours, photos of the correct state.
questions.help: Are they at the point of use, and do they match what is actually there?

questions.text: Floor markings are intact, the correct colour and match the marking standard.
questions.help: Look for worn, missing or wrong-colour tape and markings that were never laid.

questions.text: Responsibilities for 5S tasks are visible: who does what, and when.
questions.help: A rota, owner names or a board that the team actually uses.

questions.text: Everyone in the area knows the standard and can show where to find it.
questions.help: Ask two people on different shifts.

questions.text: Changes to the layout or standards follow a change process and the documents are updated.
questions.help: Check that recent changes are reflected in the standard layout and the visuals.

questions.text: Layout checks and 5S checks are done on schedule and recorded.
questions.help: Look at the check records for gaps.

questions.text: Actions from earlier checks and audits are closed on time.
questions.help: Check the action log for this area.

questions.text: The team can explain the 5S standards for the area and why they matter.
questions.help: Ask someone to talk you through their own area.

questions.text: Leaders include 5S in their walks and the results are on the board.
questions.help: Look for recent dated entries.

questions.text: Scores are stable or improving, and problems that keep coming back get a root-cause fix.
questions.help: Compare with previous audits for this area.
